Corrected admission, criterion 2: the crate-private TunnelSpec accepts a 500 ms attach budget while the stub delays its bind for 2 s. HostTunnelsConfig::default fixes the public host-forward attach budget at 5 s and ready budget at 30 s, so the same 2 s fixture does not cross that attach budget at the public route. A public reproduction would require slowing the stub beyond 5 s and would also add mandatory identity negotiation; it cannot preserve this existing short-budget control without new behavior or visibility. Keep the private establish/healthz fixture, its one-SSH/Attached/reaped assertions and supporting transport.

Corrected admission, criteria 2 and 4: the direct healthz_ok(port, ProbeLimit { deadline: now + 5 s, cancel: None }) call asserts a no-newline byte flood returns before 1 s, independently of timeout. The same test also injects ATTACH_SLICE/READY_SLICE into private TunnelSpec and asserts failed establish reaps its child. The host-forward HTTP response hides direct probe completion and uses fixed 5 s/30 s budgets plus identity negotiation; a refusal after its deadline would not prove byte-cap enforcement. Keep this private bounded-read and child-lifecycle seam; no production visibility is widened.

All 24 originally admitted function bodies match the starting HEAD byte-for-byte and pass in the 26-test library suite. Required private seams and child entry points remain. Production edits delete only cfg(test) helpers; no behavior, dependency or visibility expansion.

Empty modules and unused test support are removed, and both admission/layout documentation and the per-identity report are updated.
